“ON” Framework 1 
 
Expressing vs Impressing 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Learn to think out loud in front of a girl to 
give a glimpse of your personality. 
 
What this means: 
 
Stop trying to impress a girl.. Instead, 
focus on expressing your personality free 
from the agenda to impress. 
 
 
Big Ideas: 
 
WRONG: Its Anytime You Start Thinking 
“If Only She Knew…”

WRONG:  Thinking, Calculating, Then 
Talking 
 
Expressing is When You Cut Off the Need 
to Impress 
 
How Can I Express My Opinions, My 
Observations and My Feelings About 
Them, My Humanity 
 
Your Humanity is Your “REALNESS” 
 
The Closer You Come to Packaging Up 
Your Realness, the Closer You Come to 
Naturally Being a Charismatic Person 
 
Realness is What We Fall For 
 
Expressing =  Thinking Out Loud 
 
Trying to Impress =  Not Good Enough On 
His Own

How Can I Relay These Facts in a Way 
That Gives Her the Biggest Glimpse of My 
Humanity, My Opinions, and My 
Personality 
 
 
 
Examples: 
 
Here is of moving from impressing to 
expressing: 
 
“My boss calls me into his office, and I’m 
shitting my pants because he’s a major 
dick, the type of guy you just want to 
punch in the face, but to my surprise he 
tells me I’m getting a raise and promotion. 
So now, I’m staring at him, trying to look 
professional, but I’m like a giddy little 
school girl waiting to sneak off 
somewhere I can jump in the air and do a 
massive fist pump without anyone seeing 
me.”

The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
Instead of telling the story in away that 
relays facts that try to impress the girl, I 
told the story in a way that gave her a 
glimpse inside my mind as it was 
happening. 
 
 
Homework:  
 
For the Rest of the Day, Practice Thinking 
Out Loud

“ON” Framework 2 
 
Its Not What You Talk About, Its How 
You Talk About It 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Don’t worry about finding interesting 
things to talk about.  Just make whatever 
you’re talking about fun and interesting.  
Take the pressure of yourself to have the 
perfect thing to talk about. 
 
What this means: 
 
When you are REAL and use ANY 
conversation topic as chance to give a girl 
a glimpse of you, you’re able to make even 
the most mundane topics interesting. 
 
 
Big Ideas:

Give Her a Glimpse of You 
 
Use Conversations to Express Your 
Humanity and Your Realness 
 
Bring Her Into Your Life 
 
Realness is Attractive Because Its 
Comfortable.  Comfort is Sexy 
 
It Shows a Comfort Level in You, That Will 
Bring Out a Comfort Level in Her 
 
Make Whatever You Do Sound Interesting 
and Fun 
 
 
Examples: 
 
Here is an example of giving a girl a 
glimpse of your personality, using a 
completely mundane topic:

“It was so embarrassing, I’m walking 
today in a pair of flip flops, and I sort of 
stub by toe into the sidewalk, and trip 
forward, and now I’m like frozen, because 
I really want to look around and see if  
anyone saw, but I know that just makes it 
worse, so I’m like trying to figure out if I 
should just be casual and keep walking 
like nothing happened, or show I have a 
sense of humor and kind of laugh it off…  
So what’s the right move there?  What’s 
the cool way to handle it? 
 
 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I used a very mundane, ordinary thing 
like stubbing my toe, a way to give her 
glimpse inside my mind, and show her 
that I’m comfortable just being myself 
around her

Homework:  
 
Every Night Ask Your Self “What Did I Do 
Today?” 
 
Then Answer in a Form of an Anecdote 
that expresses your personality, and 
makes even something mundane you did 
seem worth talking about

“ON” Framework 3 
 
Co-Create the Moment 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
The magic point in a conversation where 
you’re completely ON happens when the 
conversation spotlight is brightly shining 
on both YOU and HER 
 
What this means: 
 
Always keep the conversation focused on 
you and her.  And do this by speaking in: I, 
You, We 
 
 
Big Ideas: 
 
Winning the Game is About Making Her 
Your Teammate

The Magic Happens When the Spotlight Is 
Shining on Both of You 
 
Always Be Thinking in Terms of I, You, 
We 
 
Be Conscious to Relate Whatever You’re 
Talking About Back to Her 
 
The Trick to Complimenting a Girl is to 
Always Make it About You and Her 
 
 
 
Examples: 
 
Here is an example of You and I: 
 
“When I got here, I totally forgot what you 
looked like. So when I saw you I was 
whoohoo. Ok. Cool." 
 
Or

“I went to this cool lounge Tuesday, you 
would totally like it because you could 
dress all funky. I think it’s totally your 
style. 
 
 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I made what I was talking about center 
around me and her.  And even when I was 
talking about a lounge, I made it about 
how I thought she would like it because of 
my observations about her. 
 
Here is an example of  WE: 
 
“We are such assholes.   Our kid would be 
such a dick.” 
 
Or

“I have a horrible voice, I bet though, if we 
recorded a song with the both us singing, 
maybe a monkey playing the Tambourine, 
we'd be a YouTube sensation. 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
Again I made us teammates.  Always be 
conscious to bring her into whatever 
you’re talking about. 
 
Example of complimenting her in the 
You and I method: 
 
 “You look so fucking elegant, I’d like to 
mess your hair up and see if you still look 
good.” 
 
 “You’re very intimidating in a positive 
way, I feel like I need be more mature 
around you.”

Homework:  
 
Practice Using I, You, We 
 
No matter who you have your next 
conversation with, practice using the I, 
You, We way of communicating with 
them.

“ON” Framework 5 
 
Its All About Anecdotes 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Anecdotes Are What You Use to Express 
Yourself and Get Your Personality Across 
 
What this means: 
 
You don’t express your personality by 
listing facts about yourself and what you 
like.  You express your personality by 
taking the other person inside your world 
through the use of anecdotes. 
 
These anecdotes are all around you, they 
happen every day, and don’t need to be 
some compelling action packed story.  It 
simply about packaging up YOUR 
PERSONALITY and bringing other people 
into your world.

Big Ideas: 
 
Develop the Ability to Think Anecdotally 
About Your Life 
 
It’s Not About Presenting the Other 
Person with Facts 
 
Its About Giving Them an Anecdote That 
Gives Them a Glimpse Inside Your Mind 
and World View 
 
An Anecdote Gives A Glimpse Inside Your 
Head For the Other Person to See, to 
Relate to, to Understand 
 
The Best Way to Get Information Across is 
to Wrap Up a Feeling in An Anecdote

What Was Going Through Your Mind As It 
Happened Is the Most Important Element 
of a Story and an Anecdote 
 
 
Example: 
 
Say you and a girl are talking about what 
you are studying in college.  And she asks 
you why you chose to study English. 
 
The WRONG way to answer this would be 
to list the factual reasons you chose it like 
you were good at writing, you thought it 
would be easy, you like to read, or 
whatever. 
 
Instead you want to give a girl a glimpse 
inside your mind through an anecdote. 
 
 
My VERSION to a Girl

“I chose English, I don’t even know why, it 
was probably like a fucking movie or 
something. I was stoned watching Reality 
Bites, and Ethan Hawke’s character 
seemed all cool and philosophical and I 
pictured my self laying in my dorm room, 
scribbling my deep insights into a 
notebook, in between massive bong hits.  
So essentially I owe 4 wasted years of 
college to Ethan Hawke.  What about you? 
Why did you choose to major in finance..” 
 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I brought her inside my head and kept my 
imagination running and she will have felt 
like she got to know me a lot more than if 
I simply told her why I chose the major. 
 
Homework:

Practice Thinking and Talking 
Anecdotally.  
 
After identifying (on paper) at least a half 
dozen topics that tend to come up in  
talking to girls, also think of an interesting 
story or example you can give that 
illustrates whatever point you're trying to 
make.  
 
Be on the lookout for anecdotal material 
you can use in conversations.

“ON” Framework 6 
 
Talk IN Action 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Use a conversation to paint a scene, and 
action drives a scene (and a conversation) 
forward, allowing you to gain some 
momentum. 
 
What this means: 
 
Show don’t tell. 
 
A girl will get a much better sense of your 
personality if you bring her into your 
world through action stories, then if you 
simply relate facts to her like “I’m really 
into martial arts.”

Big Ideas: 
 
You are Painting a Picture.  The better, 
more action packed the picture is, the 
easier it will be to draw her in. 
 
Once You’ve Created the Scene, You Can 
Both Add to it Very Easily 
 
It Creates Momentum 
 
It Moves the Conversation Forward 
 
The Goal of Being “ON” is to Naturally 
Move the Conversation Forward. 
  
Example: 
 
Say you and a girl are talking about your 
interest in charity. 
 
The WRONG way to approach this would 
be to say something like “Oh, you

volunteer in soup kitchens? That is 
awesome.  I’d love to do that one day too.” 
 
My VERSION to a Girl 
 
“That’s awesome, I once saw a guy give a 
homeless man a few bucks, and the 
homeless guy gets the biggest shit eating 
grin on his face, and runs up to the guy, 
I’m thinking he’s about to attack him or 
something and he gives him a giant bear 
hug. And I’m remember thinking, man, I’d 
like to people to make people happy like 
that one day.  It’s cool that you get to do 
that…  That inspires me to get off my ass.” 
 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I painted her a picture of a scene from my 
life, and she will have felt like she got to 
know me a lot more than if I simply stated 
“I want to volunteer one day too.”

Homework:  
 
Practice Talking in Action 
 
Look for ways to put whatever you want 
to say into action.   
 
Here is an example: 
 
Me:  Ballet, really that’s cool?  So like I 
have a totally warped vision of ballet 
dancers now because of black swan, I just 
imagine you all like cutting each others 
break lines, pushing each other down the 
stairs, then like, violently making out 
weight each other.  Any of that ever 
happen to you?

“ON” Framework 7 
 
Hit the Fast Forward Button 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Get in the habit of skipping over the 
boring parts of conversation and jump 
right into the “fun” and emotional realms. 
 
What this means: 
 
Some of the best, most intriguing opening 
scenes of a book or movie occur in media 
res.  Meaning “in the middle.” 
 
The same goes for conversations.  Instead 
of going through all the get to know you 
chit chat, jump right into a story or 
anecdote, or asking her opinion on 
something.

Big Ideas: 
 
Its Possible and Advantageous to Skip the 
Boring Parts 
 
Skip the Small Talk 
 
Its About Assuming Rapport 
 
You Can Always Backup Later to Fill in the 
Details 
 
Eliminate Your Need to Give Someone 
Your Back Story 
 
This Framework is About Creating the 
Illusion of Rapport 
 
Resist the Urge to Engage in Small Talk 
 
Make your goal to Just Find Out if She’s 
Cool and Easy to Talk To

Example: 
 
When you sit down on a date with a girl 
for the first time, instead of going through 
the “polite” conversation about her drive 
over, the weather, and other boring 
topics, jump right into something more 
engaging that will allow the two of you to 
express your personalities easier. 
 
 
My VERSION to a Girl 
 
“So, I’m trying to avoid this friend that 
keeps calling me, I like the guy, but he's 
just like a "user", kind of guy you know 
doesn’t have your back, so I’m driving 
over here, and he's calling...” 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I immediately brought some drama and 
gossip into a conversation that could

have easily swayed toward the boring or 
mundane small talk that most dates start 
with. 
 
Homework:  
 
Resist the Urge to Provide Back Story.  
And practice jumping to something 
interesting early on.

“ON” Framework 8 
 
Speak Your Vulnerability 
 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Being On Means Being Real, Being 
Yourself, and to Express Your Humanity. 
In order to do this, you must speak your 
vulnerabilities instead of hiding from 
them. 
 
What this means: 
 
Allow yourself to express your humanity, 
your realness, your flaws, in a confident 
way that says: “this is who I am, and I’m 
comfortable enough with myself to say 
whatever I want.”

Big Ideas: 
 
Vulnerability Humanizes You 
 
Being On Means Being Real, Being 
Yourself, and to Express Your Humanity 
 
By Expressing Your Humanity It Makes 
You Appear More Comfortable with Your 
Self 
 
Vulnerability is not about blaming or 
complaining 
 
Vulnerability is not about making a ton of 
self deprecating comments. 
 
Speaking your vulnerability is about not 
hiding who you are out of fear that you 
won’t be liked. 
 
Awkward Situations Are a Great Time To 
Express Vulnerability

Example: 
 
If you are talking to a girl who is younger 
that you, and you feel vulnerable about 
your age, instead of putting on a false 
bravado, you can simply address in a way 
that is read. 
 
Say I’m talking about birthday…  
 
My VERSION to a Girl 
 
“Yea, I turned 37 last week, for some 
reason it hit me, I started having like a 
mid life crisis panic attack. I remember 
when I was a kid, I had this one uncle, he 
was my favorite, and I remember asking 
him “how old are you?” and he was 24. 
And I still remember doing the 
calculations in my head and  thinking 
“man, you’re so old, its gonna be the year 
2000 before I turn 24”.  It blows my mind

how fast time goes.  So what’s on your 
bucket list? 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I got the age issue out of the question, but 
also used it as a chance to humanize 
myself, give the girl a glimpse inside my 
life, and show her that I’m comfortable 
enough with myself to say things that 
don’t make me look “perfect” around her. 
 
Homework:  
 
Practice Speaking Your Vulnerability 
 
Allow Yourself to not try to appear 
perfect around a girl.  Express your likes, 
desires, interests openly, even if they 
don’t make you look the standard 
definition of cool.

“ON” Framework 10 
 
Telegraph Your Punches 
 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
When You Answer Your Own Question 
From Your Own Point of View Before 
Asking It, It Allows Her to Feel More 
Comfortable Sharing and Expressing. 
 
What this means: 
 
Before asking a girl a question, share 
something or reveal something during the 
buildup to the question that will inspire  
her to have a better answer. 
 
Big Ideas:

Sharing Your Answer While Asking a 
Question Gives Her Time to Prepare an 
Answer 
 
When You Answer Your Own Question 
From Your Own Point of View Before 
Asking It, It Allows Her to Feel More 
Comfortable Sharing and Expressing 
 
Be Willing to Imagine Up a Scenario to Get 
an Emotion Across 
 
Paint a Visual Picture That Helps Her Give 
a Better Answer 
 
The Better Her Responses, the Better The 
Entire Vibe 
 
Constantly Combine Frameworks 
 
 
Example:

If you are talking to a girl and want to get 
to know her wants, aspirations, or just 
something fun or silly about her that will 
help build a connection. 
 
Say I’m about to ask her what is something 
she has always wanted to do…  
 
My VERSION to a Girl 
 
"Hey I want to learn to play chess. I want 
to be all cerebral, and calculating my 
move, just like destroying nerds (You 
mime some of this out.) What do you 
want to do that you have never done?" 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
Before asking her what she wants to do 
that she’s never done, I encouraged her to 
give a more fun and playful answer by 
first sharing my answer to the question in 
a fun, playful way.

Homework:  
 
Practice Telegraphing Your Punches 
 
Next time you want to inspire a better 
answer from someone, first, reveal 
something about yourself in the question 
that will point them in the direction you 
want the vibe of the conversation to go.

“ON” Framework 11 
 
Get Illogical 
 
 
What the framework states: 
 
Make random statements that may seem 
out of place or illogical to a conversation, 
yet Expresses Your Personality, Opinions, 
and Interests 
 
What this means: 
 
When talking to a girl, instead of trying to 
keep to a logical framework  following a 
linear conversation path, dispense 
statements that convey personality, lead 
the vibe, and demonstrate a relaxed 
confidence in who you are. 
 
Big Ideas:

A Statement Leads the vibe, and 
Expresses Your Personality, Opinions, and 
Interests 
 
Its Bold and Projects Confidence 
 
It Encourages Her to Express Her 
Personality 
 
You Can Just Say Illogical Shit. No One is 
really paying attention.  And the vibe is 
always more important than what comes 
out of your mouth. 
 
Get in the Habit of Making Statements, 
about yourself, and about her. 
 
Every time You Make a Statement About 
Yourself, You’re Giving Her Permission to 
Express 
 
Get the Vibe Right, and Nothing Else 
Matters

All People Want to Talk About is Stupid 
Fun Shit  
 
 
Example: 
 
If you are talking to a girl and feel the 
conversation is taking a turn towards the 
logical, blurt something out completely 
unexpected. 
 
 
Random Things I’ve Said to Girls 
 
I hate old people. I know one day I’ll be 
old, blah blah. 
 
I want to be rich. I know its not PC or 
whatever to admit that and I should like  
talk about passion or whatever, but 
honestly, I really like having nice shit.   
You don’t strike me as materialistic.

I’m obsessed with corn dogs. Like if 
someone tells me a diner has a good corn 
dog, I’ll like do a road trip.  I don’t take 
you as the type of girl who likes corn 
dogs. 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I just said random statements about 
myself to keep things from getting too 
much toward a logical level. 
 
 
Homework:  
 
Begin Leading With Statements About 
Yourself 
 
Next time you to break the “logic trap” of 
a conversation blurt out the first random 
statement that comes to mind.  Don’t 
censor yourself, let it become a skill to 
“think outloud”.

“ON” Framework 12 
 
The More You Give The More You Get 
 
What the framework states: 
 
If you want to get a woman opening up 
and making the conversation come more 
easily, you must first open up to her, and 
give more than you’re getting. 
 
What this means: 
 
When talking to a girl, take the initiative 
to introduce new “emotions” or threads 
into a conversation.  Don’t wait for her to 
tell you its OK. 
 
Big Ideas: 
 
A Lot of Time She’s Not Good At It, And 
She’s Waiting for You to Take the Lead

Making the Effort Yourself Snaps Her Into 
And Takes You From a Dry Conversation 
to a Fun One Very Quickly 
 
It Encourages Her to Express Her 
Personality 
 
You Gain Rapport Quicker and Easier the 
Less Formal You Are 
 
Before You Ask An Intimate Question, You 
Need to Reveal Something Intimate First 
 
Always Give Her Just Enough to Grab Onto 
Something 
 
When You Push The Line, Your Showing 
Her You’re Not Afraid to Be Real Around 
Her. Being Real Around Someone is a Very 
Attractive Quality

It Gives Her a Chance to Relate Back 
 
 
 
Example: 
 
If you are talking to a girl and the 
conversation is in a neutral “PG” realm 
where neither of you have really let your 
guards down around each other, bring 
something into the conversation that 
allows her to feel like she’s gotten a sneak 
peak inside your  head. 
 
THINK:  How Can I Give Just a Little More 
Than What They Asked of Me? 
 
 
Putting this idea into action 
 
“I hate old people, lets go find some old 
people and people beat them up. I went 
out on a date with an old woman once. It

was so awkward. I met her at a lounge, it 
was dark, and apparently I was very 
drunk.  We sit down for dinner,  and listen 
I’m not an ageist or anything, but I’m not 
talking like oh she was 40 I was 35… I’m 
talking menopausal old woman.  The 
worse part was, at the end of the date, I 
kind of feel like I have to kiss her, because 
you know she paid for dinner…” 
 
The Reality of What I Just Said. 
 
I brought a pretty unexpected story into 
the conversation that showed a comfort 
in straying into “forbidden” conversation 
territory. 
 
 
Homework:  
 
Practice Revealing Just a Little Bit More 
Than You Normally Would
